observation.visible_scene: A close-up view of a stainless steel cooking pot sitting on a stovetop burner. The pot holds a pale yellowish liquid that is at a vigorous, rolling boil, with foam and bubbles churning across the surface and wisps of steam rising above it. The inner wall shows etched volume markings (3.5, 4, 5 Qt Max) and two rivet heads; a handle projects to the lower left and another to the upper right. The background is softly blurred, showing warm brown kitchen tones and an indistinct light-colored shape at the top.
visible_changes: The liquid remains in continuous active boiling throughout the excerpt; bubble clusters and foam patches form, break, and reform on the surface without the process starting or stopping within the clip.

The surface pattern shifts over time: in the early-to-mid frames a clearer yellowish pool is visible near the center with foam concentrated toward the edges, while in the later frames the froth spreads and the surface appears more uniformly white and bubbly.
Steam plumes drift upward and vary in density from frame to frame above the boiling surface.
The pot and its handles stay in essentially the same position in the frame across the clip, with only minor apparent framing differences.
No object is added to or removed from the pot during the excerpt; the contents appear to be the same boiling liquid throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: The identity of the liquid and any food items submerged within it are not established.
The heat source setting and what triggered the boil are not shown.
What happens after the excerpt ends (whether the boil subsides or the pot is emptied) is unknown.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain; the pot's framing is nearly constant, so any slight shifts may be handheld jitter rather than deliberate movement.
The blurred light-colored shape at the top of the frame (possibly a person's arm or background object) cannot be identified.
Whether the increased froth in later frames reflects a true change in boiling intensity or just momentary foam distribution is not determinable from the frames alone.
